title: MIDI
summary: MIDI is a technical standard enabling electronic musical instruments, computers, and audio devices to communicate performance data. A single MIDI cable carries up to sixteen channels of data, where each interaction with a controller converts into a MIDI event specifying pitch, timing, and velocity. These events can trigger sound modules or be recorded into sequencers. Before MIDI, instruments used proprietary interfaces like CV/gate; MIDI allowed cross-manufacturer compatibility. The standard was developed in 1983 by industry representatives and is maintained by the MIDI Manufacturers Association.

mechanisms.title: Event-based communication protocol
mechanisms.explanation: Each key press, knob turn, or slider movement is converted into a MIDI event. These events encapsulate musical instructions such as a note's pitch, timing, and velocity. The protocol transmits these discrete messages rather than audio signals, allowing for flexible routing and editing.

mechanisms.title: Multi-channel data transmission
mechanisms.explanation: A single physical MIDI cable can carry up to sixteen independent channels of MIDI data. Each channel can be routed to a separate device, enabling a single controller to play multiple instruments simultaneously or manage complex setups without additional cabling.
